thread:
Samira: Morning all — quick async check-in for day 3. What I did: completed laptop setup, ran `./bootstrap.sh`, linked GitHub account, and grabbed the dev env creds from the console. Blockers: 1) trying to access s3://redwood-dev-config but get 403; 2) SSH to bastion fails with \"Permission denied (publickey)\". Also Docker login on my M1 kept failing with x509 cert error.

Alex: hey Samira — for the S3 403 can you confirm which profile you used? `aws sts get-caller-identity --profile redwood-dev` should show your ARN. If it's not your user, the ACLs won't allow access. Also check that your IAM role is attached via Okta group.

Samira: ran `aws sts get-caller-identity --profile redwood-dev` and got a role arn: `arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/temporary-ci-role/session` — hmm looks like it picked up the CI role instead of my user creds.

Priya: that explains the 403. You likely have `~/.aws/credentials` entries for `ci` and `redwood-dev`. Try `export AWS_PROFILE=samira-dev` then re-run, or remove the CI profile temporarily. If that still fails, ping IT to ensure your Okta group is in the S3 access policy.

Samira: thanks — will try that now. Also, SSH error: `ssh -i ~/.ssh/id_rsa ubuntu@bastion.redwood.internal` -> `Permission denied (publickey)`. I uploaded the public key in the console under \"SSH keys\".

Alex: two things to check: 1) make sure the key you uploaded matches `ssh-keygen -lf ~/.ssh/id_rsa.pub`; 2) bastion uses `ubuntu` user but we recently rotated to `redwood-bastion` in some accounts — try `ssh -i ~/.ssh/id_rsa ubuntu@bastion.redwood.internal -vvv` to see which key is offered. Example debug: ```ssh -i ~/.ssh/id_rsa -vvv ubuntu@bastion.redwood.internal```

Samira: ran the `-vvv`. It shows my key isn't being offered; found that my key file permissions were 0644. Fixed to 0600 and re-tried, still no dice.

Priya: if permissions were the issue it's usually `Permission denied` but if it's still failing maybe the key wasn't actually registered in the right account. Can you verify the key fingerprint in the console UI vs `ssh-keygen -lf` output? If mismatch, re-upload. If it matches, open a quick IT ticket with the subject: \"SSH key not accepted on bastion — Samira\" and paste the fingerprint.

Samira: opened IT ticket #5481 (submitted via internal portal). Ticket includes fingerprint and `-vvv` output.

DevOnboardBot: Provisioning step 4 completed for user Samira — added to `dev-team` Okta group. 

IT Support: saw ticket #5481 — adding Samira's key to bastion-authorized in the dev account now, should be live in ~15m. Also verifying S3 policy membership.

Samira: awesome, thanks — will re-test in 20m. Also, tiny follow-ups: asked for a code-review ping on PR #72 (frontend nav tweak), and curious whether anyone can share the local env `.env.example` secrets mapping?

Alex: pinged on PR #72 — left a small comment. For `.env.example` check `doc/dev-environment.md` (link: https://internal.redwood/doc/dev-environment) — the secrets mapping is listed under \"Local secrets\" section.

Priya: regarding Docker/M1 x509 issue — try `export DOCKER_BUILDKIT=0` as a workaround, and update to Docker Desktop 4.9+ which includes fixes. If it keeps happening, attach the error output to the IT ticket and we'll triage.

Samira: re-tested after IT update — SSH now works, can access the bastion and forwarded through to the dev host. S3 still 403 for one bucket but I can access the others. Leaving this as partial-blocker until IT confirms bucket-level ACLs. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

Alex: great progress — if S3 issue persists after IT confirms, post here and we'll escalate to infra.

Samira: will do. Today plan: finish PR #72, run through the quickstart app, and start the eval harness tutorial.

Priya: welcome again — let us know if you want a quick pairing session for the eval harness later today.

Samira: would love that, thanks!
